transparency_notes: Release full SubstClus inventories (cluster membership per target), code for multi-view NMF runs (including λ settings and initialization seeds), and the exact sampled 1000 AGiga sentences used for each target to enable reproduction.
Provide trained AddCos word/context embeddings and scripts used to compute AddCos scores (with random seeds and training logs) so context view can be reproduced.
Publish full per-target B-Cubed scores, per-inventory coverage statistics, per-inventory GAP distributions, and scripts to compute Oracle and Best-Fit GAP values.

creativity_safeguard.novelty_not_validity_note: The inclusion of an explicit, aggregated context-substitutability view into a multi-view clustering objective appears to be a novel framing relative to prior PPDB clustering work; however novelty is orthogonal to empirical validity — the method still requires rigorous robustness analyses (sensitivity, statistical tests, and disentangling WSD) to substantiate utility.
counterfactual_conditions_for_success: If AddCos computed on a sufficiently large and domain-representative sentence sample reliably approximates human substitutability across many targets, then the context view will drive clusters toward human-like substitutability and extrinsic GAP improvements will generalize.
If k-selection and PPDB cutoff are robust (stable across reasonable ranges) and inventories are not overfitted to CoInCo, multi-view SubstClus should outperform PPDBClus broadly.
If WSD can be improved (even modestly) beyond the simple best-fit heuristic, Best-Fit GAP will approach Oracle GAP and demonstrate the practical utility of SubstClus for downstream systems.
If translation probabilities in PPDB are sufficiently dense and language-diverse for many targets, the T view can improve disambiguation for senses that are translation-distinct.

novelty_lenses.rationale: Elevating substitutability to an explicit data view and integrating it into a multi-view clustering pipeline creates a tighter coupling between intrinsic sense structure and extrinsic lexsub performance—this reframes sense clustering objectives toward downstream utility rather than pure lexical relatedness.
evidence: Sec.3.1.1 defines the context-substitutability view using AddCos aggregated across sentences, directly linking clustering features to substitutability.
Sec.5 links oracle/best-fit GAP experiments to the substitutability metric to show downstream relevance.
uncertainty_flags: Empirical validation is incomplete without per-inventory B-Cubed numbers, sensitivity analyses, and correlation statistics; conceptual novelty does not yet have fully quantified empirical support.

novelty_lenses.rationale: Technically the work combines known components—PPDB signals, translation proxies, WordNet embeddings, multi-view NMF, and AddCos—so in engineering terms it is an integration and adaptation rather than wholly new algorithmic machinery. The primary novelty is the specific objective alignment (substitutability) and the engineering to scale it to PPDB.
evidence: Manuscript builds on Liu et al. (2013) multi-view NMF and Cocos & Callison-Burch (2016) PPDBClus as baselines, while adding the C view and applied evaluation chain (Sec.3, Sec.4).
uncertainty_flags: Degree of conceptual novelty depends on how unique the C view formulation is relative to prior context-sensitive clustering attempts; without a survey of close precedents, novelty magnitude is somewhat uncertain.

confidence_interval.rationale: I am moderately confident that the conceptual contribution (making substitutability an explicit clustering view and linking intrinsic substitutability to extrinsic lexsub filtering) is sound and potentially impactful based on the described methodology and reported qualitative/aggregate results. However the absence of full numeric B-Cubed tables, sensitivity analyses, statistical tests, and explicit WSD accuracy lowers confidence about the magnitude and generality of the empirical claims; thus a mid-range confidence interval is appropriate.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The paper proposes SubstClus: a multi-view NMF-based clustering pipeline that combines a Context Substitutability view (AddCos scores on sampled sentences), PPDB2.0 paraphrase similarity, shared translation probabilities, and WordNet-synset affinities to induce substitutable paraphrase sense clusters from PPDB. The clusters are evaluated intrinsically via an extended B-Cubed F-score (β=0.5) against CoInCo lexsub annotations and extrinsically by using inventories as filters on rankings produced by Syn.VSM and AddCos. Main claims are (1) multi-view SubstClus yields more substitutable and higher-coverage inventories than prior automatic inventories and is comparable/better than WordNet/TWSI on average; (2) inventories improve lexsub GAP under oracle and (to a lesser extent) best-fit WSD; (3) the B-Cubed substitutability metric predicts Oracle GAP potential; (4) views are complementary and multi-view outperforms single-view, though nouns remain challenging. The manuscript provides qualitative examples, Table 2 baseline B-Cubed numbers, Table 5 GAP results for various SubstClus variants and baselines, and descriptions of implementation choices (PPDB cutoff 2.3, 1000 sampled sentences, λi=0.01, k∈[2,10] selected by Silhouette on XP). However, key quantitative links are underspecified: per-variant substitutability (B-Cubed) numbers for all SubstClus variants are not tabulated; correlation statistics between substitutability and Oracle/Best-Fit GAP are not reported; WSD heuristic accuracy is not provided; and sensitivity analyses / statistical significance testing are missing. These gaps leave uncertainty about effect sizes, robustness to hyperparameters, and the degree to which filtering gains stem from inventory quality versus WSD or lexsub model properties.
logical_argument_graph: A1: PPDB provides many paraphrase candidates; but they are noisy and polysemous, so clustering by sense can help lexsub.
A2: Construct four views (C: AddCos context fit; P: PPDB2.0 scores; T: shared translations; W: WordNet synset affinity) to capture complementary signals related to substitutability.

A3: Use multi-view NMF (with λi=0.01) to find consensus clusters; pick k via Silhouette computed on XP (PPDB-paraphrase view) over k∈{2..10}; restrict paraphrases to PPDB score ≥ 2.3; sample 1000 AGiga sentences for C view.
A4: Evaluate clusters intrinsically via extended B-Cubed F-score (β=0.5) against CoInCo annotations to measure 'substitutability' per-target and averaged over targets.

A5: Demonstrate SubstClus clusters are more substitutable than baselines (WordNet+, PPDBClus, TWSI) and have greater coverage than WordNet via intrinsic measures and coverage statistics (Table 2 for baselines; SubstClus numbers claimed but not fully tabulated).
A6: Apply inventories as filters to lexsub rankings (Syn.VSM and AddCos) and measure Unfiltered, Oracle-Filtered, and Best-Fit (simple WSD) GAP to show extrinsic utility (Table 5).
A7: Show Oracle GAP correlates qualitatively with B-Cubed substitutability, implying substitutability predicts potential lexsub improvement; Best-Fit GAP < Oracle GAP highlights WSD limitations.

A8: Ablations (single-view vs multi-view) qualitatively indicate complementarity and that multi-view inventories outperform single-view ones; POS split indicates noun-specific weakness where TWSI is strong.

identified_claims.claim_text: A multi-view clustering method incorporating Context Substitutability (AddCos), Paraphrase Similarity (PPDB2.0), Shared Translations, and WordNet synset similarity produces paraphrase sense clusters that are more substitutable (per extended B-Cubed F-score) and have wider coverage than prior automatically-derived inventories (e.g., PPDBClus) and are comparable/better than WordNet/TWSI on average across parts of speech.
evidence: Sec. 4.3 states all multiview inventories and SubstClusP single-view are more substitutable than WordNet and TWSI per B-Cubed.
Table 2 provides baseline B-Cubed scores for WordNet+, TWSI, PPDBClus, showing PPDBClus has lower substitutability.
Sec. 6 and Table 5 show GAP performance where SubstClus inventories often outperform baselines in Oracle and Best-Fit GAP aggregated over POS.
uncertainty_flags: Per-variant numeric B-Cubed scores for SubstClus variants are not tabulated in the main text; claim relies on textual statement rather than full numeric evidence.
Coverage claims for SubstClus (e.g., 'wider coverage than WordNet') are asserted, but explicit per-variant coverage statistics are missing from main tables.

identified_claims.claim_label: SubstClus improves lexsub rankings via filtering
identified_claims.claim_text: SubstClus inventories can be used to filter outputs of lexsub ranking models (Syn.VSM, AddCos) to substantially improve oracle and practical (best-fit with a simple WSD heuristic) GAP scores.
evidence: Table 4 shows a sentence-level example where SubstClusCPWT filtering raised AddCos GAP from 0.47 to 0.78.
Table 5 reports Unfiltered, Oracle, Best-Fit GAP averages across inventories and models; many SubstClus variants show higher Oracle and Best-Fit GAP compared to unfiltered and PPDBClus in aggregate.
uncertainty_flags: Best-Fit improvements depend strongly on simple WSD heuristic; Best-Fit GAP remains notably below Oracle GAP implying realized gains are limited by WSD quality.
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals reported for GAP improvements; effect sizes and variability across targets are unclear.

identified_claims.claim_text: The extended B-Cubed F-score substitutability metric is predictive of an inventory's potential to improve lexsub (Oracle GAP correlates with substitutability), though WSD quality limits realized gains (Best-Fit GAP < Oracle GAP).
evidence: Sec. 2 formalizes substitutability as average extended B-Cubed (β=0.5) over targets.
Sec. 6 states that comparing B-Cubed to Oracle GAP shows substitutability is a good indicator; inventories scoring high in B-Cubed also score high in Oracle GAP.
uncertainty_flags: No quantitative correlation statistics (Pearson/Spearman) or p-values are provided, so the strength of the relationship is not quantified.
Choice of β=0.5 biases metric toward precision; sensitivity of correlation to β not explored.

identified_claims.claim_text: Different combinations of views yield complementary benefits; multi-view solutions outperform single-view baselines, and the method generalizes across POS though noun performance may require special treatment (TWSI remains strong on nouns).
evidence: Sec. 3 defines four views and rationale.
Experiments include single-view and multi-view variants (SubstClusC, P, W, T, CP, CPW, CPWT) and Figure 1 displays example clusters across views.
Sec. 6 notes multi-view inventories exceed baselines overall, but TWSI beats others on nouns.
uncertainty_flags: Per-view ablation numeric results (B-Cubed per view and ablation GAP deltas) are not clearly tabulated, so the magnitude of each view's contribution is unclear.
POS-specific evaluation is reported in Table 5 for nouns vs all-words, but deeper diagnostic analysis is missing.

identified_claims.claim_text: Multi-view NMF with λi=0.01, PPDB score cutoff 2.3, 1000 sampled AGiga sentences for the C view, and k selected from 2–10 via Silhouette on XP yields effective clustering for targets.
evidence: Sec. 3.1.1 describes XS built from 1000 AGiga sentences; AddCos used for entries.
Sec. 4.2 states PPDB cutoff 2.3 chosen based on CoInCo train tuning; k chosen by maximizing Silhouette on XP over 2..10.
A.2 specifies multi-view NMF objective and λi=0.01.
uncertainty_flags: Sensitivity analyses for these hyperparameters are not reported; robustness to PPDB cutoff, XS size, λi, and k-range is untested.
Choosing k via Silhouette on XP may bias solution toward PPDB structure rather than context substitutability; the effect is not quantified.

strengths.title: Clear, task-aligned multi-view design
strengths.description: The paper intentionally combines complementary signals (contextual substitutability, PPDB scores, translations, WordNet) to target substitutability, aligning method design with the lexsub application.
evidence: Sec. 3 enumerates four views and justifies each in relation to substitutability.
Multi-view NMF is used to seek consensus clustering across views (Sec. 3.1).

strengths.title: Practical extrinsic evaluation linking intrinsic metric to downstream benefit
strengths.description: Authors evaluate inventories both intrinsically (extended B-Cubed) and extrinsically (Oracle and Best-Fit GAP on lexsub), demonstrating a concrete application and showing potential improvements.
evidence: Sec. 2 defines substitutability metric; Sec. 5 describes oracle and best-fit filtering experiments; Table 5 reports GAP results.

strengths.title: Operationalized substitutability metric
strengths.description: The use of extended B-Cubed with β=0.5 is a principled way to quantify substitutability against CoInCo annotations and makes the intrinsic objective explicit.
evidence: Sec. 2 and Appendix A.1 provide formal definition and rationale for using B-Cubed and β=0.5.

strengths.title: Scalable implementation choices
strengths.description: The method uses large precompiled resources (PPDB2.0 XXL, AGiga embeddings) and an automated pipeline (1000 sampled sentences) making it scalable across many targets.
evidence: Sec. 3.1.1 describes sampling from AGiga; A.3 describes training word/context embeddings on AGiga; PPDB2.0-XXL used as candidate pool (Sec. 4.2).

concerns.title: Missing per-variant substitutability numbers
concerns.description: The manuscript claims SubstClus variants outperform baselines on substitutability, but numeric extended B-Cubed F-scores per SubstClus variant (C/P/W/T/CP/CPW/CPWT) are not presented, preventing direct verification of intrinsic effect sizes.
evidence: Shared analysis and Sec. 4.3 assert multiview inventories are more substitutable, but the only explicit B-Cubed numbers given are for baselines in Table 2 (WordNet+, TWSI, PPDBClus).
Prior-stage digests repeatedly note absence of per-variant B-Cubed table.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Add a table listing subst(C,L) (extended B-Cubed β=0.5) for every inventory evaluated (all SubstClus variants and baselines), with standard errors or CIs computed (e.g., bootstrap over targets).

concerns.title: No statistical testing or variability estimates for GAP improvements
concerns.description: Reported Unfiltered/Oracle/Best-Fit GAP averages (Table 5) lack confidence intervals, per-target variance, or statistical significance tests, so it is unclear whether observed improvements are robust.
evidence: Table 5 presents average GAPs but no SE/CI or p-values; text claims improvements but does not provide statistical corroboration.
Prior-stage reviewers flagged the absence of variance estimates and significance testing.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide per-inventory GAP standard deviations, bootstrap confidence intervals, and pairwise significance tests (e.g., paired bootstrap) comparing filtered vs unfiltered and against baselines for both Oracle and Best-Fit conditions.

concerns.title: Unquantified correlation between substitutability and Oracle/Best-Fit GAP
concerns.description: The paper asserts that B-Cubed predicts Oracle GAP potential qualitatively, but offers no correlation coefficients or tests to quantify this association.
evidence: Sec. 6 states inventories with high B-Cubed also have high Oracle GAP but no Pearson/Spearman values or scatterplots are reported.
Shared analysis recommends reporting correlation statistics.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Compute and report Pearson and Spearman correlations between per-target B-Cubed and Oracle GAP (and Best-Fit GAP), include scatterplots and significance tests, and analyze sensitivity to β.

concerns.title: No sensitivity analysis of key hyperparameters
concerns.description: Critical choices (PPDB cutoff 2.3, 1000 sampled sentences for C view, λi=0.01, k-range and Silhouette-on-XP for k selection) are reasonable but untested for robustness; outcomes may depend heavily on these choices.
evidence: Sec. 4.2 mentions threshold 2.3 tuned on CoInCo train but offers no cross-validation or alternate-threshold results; A.2 lists λi=0.01 as default without exploration.
Shared analysis emphasizes lack of hyperparameter sensitivity studies.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report sensitivity experiments varying PPDB cutoff (e.g., 1.5, 2.0, 2.3, 3.0), XS sample sizes (e.g., 250, 500, 1000, 2000), λi values (e.g., 0.001, 0.01, 0.1), and alternative k-selection strategies (e.g., Silhouette on C or combined views). Present effect on B-Cubed and GAP.

concerns.title: Conflation of inventory quality and WSD performance in Best-Fit GAP
concerns.description: Best-Fit GAP uses a simple heuristic (majority sense among top-5 model-ranked substitutes) whose accuracy is not reported; without measuring WSD accuracy, Best-Fit GAP cannot separate inventory utility from disambiguation effectiveness.
evidence: Sec. 5.4 describes best-fit heuristic but no WSD accuracy figures are provided.
Sec. 6 notes Best-Fit < Oracle but does not quantify WSD errors' contribution.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report accuracy of the Best-Fit heuristic (proportion of sentences where heuristic chooses the same sense as oracle), and/or compare Best-Fit GAP using stronger WSD methods or a controlled partial-oracle to quantify contribution of WSD errors.

concerns.title: Incomplete per-view ablation numbers
concerns.description: Although single-view and multi-view experiments are run, the manuscript lacks a fine-grained numeric ablation table quantifying each view's marginal contribution to B-Cubed and GAP.
evidence: Figure 1 gives qualitative cluster examples; Table 5 reports overall GAP for variants but not per-view intrinsic B-Cubed values or effect sizes.
Sec. 4.2 mentions experiments with seven combinations but detailed numeric ablation is missing.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide a table with per-view and incremental ablation results: B-Cubed and Oracle/Best-Fit GAP for C, P, W, T individually and for combinations, with variance estimates.

concerns.title: Lack of reproducibility artifacts and inventory release
concerns.description: Claims about generated inventories' coverage and extrinsic utility require release of inventories, sampled sentences for C view, trained embeddings and code to reproduce multi-view NMF runs; the manuscript does not state whether these artifacts will be shared.
evidence: Shared analysis and chaining notes request exact artifacts; manuscript does not include link or mention of release.
Paper depends on various data processing choices (PPDB subset thresholding, sampled AGiga sentences, NMF initialization) that affect results.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide a public release (or supplementary archive) of SubstClus inventories (all variants), scripts/configs for multi-view NMF, sampled XS sentences, trained embeddings, and evaluation scripts with seeds to enable reproducibility.

comparable_works.relevance: Direct baseline: prior automatic clustering of PPDB paraphrases by sense using spectral clustering and PPDB2.0 scores.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Similar in using PPDB paraphrases and paraphrase scores; differs by adding context substitutability, translations, WordNet view, and using multi-view NMF instead of spectral clustering.
comparable_works.source_trace: Manuscript cites Cocos and Callison-Burch (2016) (multiple sections: introduction, Sec. 3; Table 2)

comparable_works.relevance: Crowdsourced noun sense inventory designed for substitutability; strong baseline for nouns.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: TWSI is human-centric and noun-focused; SubstClus aims for automated, high-coverage inventories across POS and claims TWSI still best for nouns.

comparable_works.relevance: Used as the Context Substitutability view and as a ranking baseline in lexsub experiments.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: AddCos provides context-fit scores used as features; here it is repurposed as direct view input to clustering and baseline ranking model.

comparable_works.relevance: Source of paraphrase candidates and PPDB2.0 score used as P view and for translation probabilities.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: PPDB used as resource; the paper augments it with additional views and clustering.

uncertainty_flags: Per-variant intrinsic substitutability (extended B-Cubed) numbers for SubstClus variants are missing; magnitude of intrinsic improvement is uncertain.
No correlation coefficients reported for B-Cubed vs Oracle/Best-Fit GAP; strength of predictive claim is qualitative.
Lack of statistical significance / confidence intervals for GAP changes across inventories.
Sensitivity of results to PPDB cutoff, XS sample size, λi, k-selection strategy, and AddCos embedding training choices is untested.
WSD heuristic accuracy is unreported, conflating inventory quality with disambiguation performance in Best-Fit GAP.
alternative_interpretations: Observed Oracle GAP gains could be primarily driven by the PPDB paraphrase-paraphrase structure (P view) and PPDB cutoff rather than the Context Substitutability view; without per-view effect sizes this remains possible.
Improvements in average GAP may be concentrated on a subset of targets with many annotator-overlapping paraphrases; average reporting may mask uneven gains and target-specific failures.

The Silhouette-on-XP k-selection may bias cluster granularity toward PPDB score topology; higher B-Cubed may reflect better alignment to PPDB-internal structure rather than genuine context-based substitutability.

Best-Fit GAP shortfall could indicate the inventory is useful but practical WSD methods used for selection are too weak; thus inventory utility might be higher if combined with better WSD, not necessarily a shortcoming of the inventory itself.
transparency_notes: Essential reproducibility artifacts (SubstClus inventories for each variant, sampled AGiga sentences, trained embeddings, code for multi-view NMF and evaluation scripts) are not linked or indicated as released; providing them would reduce uncertainty.
Implementation details (random seeds, initialization, NMF convergence criteria, computational resources) are only partially specified in supplemental text; more exact configs help reproduce results.
Choice of β=0.5 in extended B-Cubed is disclosed (Appendix A.1) but its sensitivity is not explored; reporting results under alternative β values would increase transparency.

creativity_safeguard.novelty_not_validity_note: Incorporating an explicit context-based substitutability view into multi-view clustering for paraphrase sense induction is a relatively novel operationalization, but novelty alone does not guarantee robustness; missing quantitative specifics limit evaluation of validity.
counterfactual_conditions_for_success: If AddCos scores accurately reflect human context substitutability across a wide variety of targets and senses, the C view will meaningfully steer clusters toward human-like substitutability.

If PPDB2.0 scoring and translations provide sufficiently complementary signals (high precision) and hyperparameters (PPDB cutoff, k-selection) are robust, multi-view consensus will reduce noise and improve substitutability.
If stronger WSD (than the simple best-fit heuristic) is used at inference time, Best-Fit GAP could approach Oracle GAP, demonstrating practical utility beyond oracle demonstrations.

novelty_lenses.rationale: Combines existing components (PPDB, AddCos, multi-view NMF, translation signals, WordNet) in a task-focused way; novelty lies in treating substitutability as an explicit view and linking intrinsic substitutability to extrinsic lexsub filtering.
evidence: Multi-view NMF (Liu et al., 2013) and PPDB clustering (Cocos & C-B 2016) are prior work; the C view and end-to-end demonstration for lexsub are new in combination.
uncertainty_flags: Novelty does not address whether empirical gains are robust — missing numeric intrinsic scores and sensitivity analyses weaken confidence in impact.

novelty_lenses.rationale: If subst(C,L) reliably predicts Oracle GAP and inventories can be widely shared and paired with effective WSD, the approach could materially improve lexsub systems; current evidence lacks the statistical and robustness reporting required to confirm practical disruption.
evidence: Table 5 shows Oracle GAP improvements across inventories suggesting potential; but Best-Fit GAP remains below Oracle and WSD is simplistic.
uncertainty_flags: No statistical testing, per-target variability, or robust WSD experiments are reported, making generalization uncertain.

confidence_interval.rationale: I provide analytic judgments and flagged uncertainties but refrain from an accept/reject decision per instructions. The interval [0,1] reflects epistemic humility: many claims are plausible and partially supported by evidence in the manuscript, but missing quantitative details (per-variant B-Cubed, correlation stats, sensitivity analyses, significance testing, WSD accuracy) leave substantial uncertainty about effect sizes and robustness.

consensus_findings: The paper presents a coherent, well-documented multi-view pipeline (multi-view NMF) combining a Context Substitutability view (AddCos), PPDB paraphrase scores, shared translations, and WordNet affinities to produce sense clusters from PPDB and evaluates them both intrinsically and extrinsically.

Intrinsic/extrinsic evaluation linkage is conceptually sound: the authors define substitutability via an extended B-Cubed F-score and demonstrate downstream relevance by using inventories to filter lexical substitution rankings (Unfiltered / Oracle / Best-Fit GAP).

Reported results and qualitative examples indicate the multi-view approach yields practical improvements (notably in Oracle GAP) relative to automatic baselines such as PPDBClus, and the method appears scalable (uses PPDB, AGiga-trained embeddings, and automated pipelines).

Multiple reviewers agree that the context/substitutability view is a meaningful and potentially novel contribution when integrated into a multi-view clustering objective targeted at lexical substitution utility.

All reviewers request additional quantitative detail and robustness analyses to establish effect sizes and generality (per-inventory B-Cubed numbers, coverage tables, statistical tests, hyperparameter sensitivity, WSD accuracy).
disagreements: Novelty assessment: some reviewers frame the contribution as an innovative integration that meaningfully reframes sense induction toward substitutability (novel conceptual signal), while others treat it as an incremental engineering combination of existing components (multi-view NMF, PPDB, AddCos, translations, WordNet).

Magnitude and generality of empirical gains: one reviewer (novelty-assessor-incremental) is relatively confident the method yields meaningful incremental advances given the presented GAP tables, whereas others emphasize that missing numeric intrinsic scores and lack of statistical testing significantly limit claims about magnitude and robustness.

Appropriate emphasis for revisions: methodology-focused reviewers prioritize reproducibility artifacts and statistical analyses, while novelty-focused reviewers prioritize conceptual framing and broader implications; these lead to different prioritizations in requested follow-up work.
uncertainty_hotspots: Absence of explicit per-inventory intrinsic substitutability values: numeric extended B-Cubed F-score (β=0.5) for every SubstClus variant and baseline is not tabulated—prevents direct verification of C1.

Missing coverage statistics for SubstClus variants: |T|, average synonyms per target, average senses per target, and overlap with CoInCo analogous to Table 2 are not reported—clouds the 'wider coverage' claim.

No statistical tests or uncertainty estimates reported for GAP results (Oracle/Best-Fit/Unfiltered): lacking variance, confidence intervals, or paired significance tests leaves robustness of observed gains unclear.

Unquantified correlation between substitutability (B-Cubed) and Oracle/Best-Fit GAP: no Pearson/Spearman coefficients, p-values, scatterplots, or regression diagnostics are presented to substantiate the predictive claim (C3).

Hyperparameter sensitivity is untested: PPDB score cutoff (2.3), number of sampled sentences for the C view (1000), λi (0.01), k-selection range and criterion (Silhouette on XP) lack ablations—results could be dependent on these choices.

Confounding of inventory quality and WSD performance: Best-Fit GAP uses a simple heuristic whose accuracy is unreported; without measuring WSD selection accuracy, Best-Fit results conflate inventory utility and disambiguation effectiveness.

Potential k-selection bias: choosing k by maximizing Silhouette on the PPDB view (XP) may bias clusters toward PPDB-internal structure rather than context-driven substitutability, possibly inflating apparent benefits of P-centric signals.

Validity of AddCos as the C-view proxy: using AddCos scores aggregated over sampled AGiga sentences assumes alignment with human substitutability; reviewers request empirical validation (e.g., correlation with CoInCo annotator data).
Translation view sparsity/noise: contribution and coverage of the translations view (XF) are not quantified; sparse or noisy translation signals could hurt or have limited impact without diagnostics.
model_diversity_effects: Role-driven focus produced complementary critique sets: structure_analyst emphasized logical coherence and missing numeric chains (per-variant subst scores); methodology_auditor stressed reproducibility, sensitivity analyses, and statistical testing; novelty assessors highlighted both conceptual originality (C-view) and the need to quantify empirical impact.

These role differences increased coverage of evaluation blind spots: where one reviewer saw acceptable detail, another flagged missing quantitative evidence—this multiplicity surfaces methodological risks (overfitting to CoInCo, hyperparameter dependence) and interpretation risks (inventory vs WSD conflation).

Divergent novelty judgments reflect the trade-off between conceptual framing (making substitutability an explicit view) and reuse of established tools: reviewers who prioritized disruptive potential focused on framing, while others prioritized empirical rigor and reproducibility.

Because reviewers used different lenses, the synthesis preserves controlled disagreement: reviewers converge on what to fix (more data, stats, ablations) while differing on how novel the assembly is; this diversity strengthens the set of targeted follow-up analyses.
meta_review.editor_guidance: Center the editorial decision on whether the authors can and should be asked to supply targeted empirical and transparency additions that are necessary to validate the paper's empirical claims. Insufficiently transparent aspects (requested): Per-inventory intrinsic substitutability numeric values for all SubstClus variants, per-inventory coverage statistics analogous to Table 2, per-target GAP distributions and variance estimates, hyperparameter sweep results, correlation statistics between B-Cubed and GAP, WSD heuristic accuracy, and concrete provenance artifacts (SubstClus inventories, sampled sentences, trained embeddings, NMF configs and seeds) are not currently available in the manuscript and are necessary for full verification and replication.
epistemic_limits: Synthesis is constrained by reviewers' inability to run experiments or access the authors' artifacts; judgments rely on the manuscript's reported tables, text statements, and appendices. Where numeric evidence is absent (per-variant B-Cubed, coverage tables, statistical tests), reviewers identifed plausible interpretations but could not disambiguate which interpretation holds in the data. Reviewers also noted potential methodological couplings that the manuscript did not quantify (e.g., AddCos used both as a view and as a baseline ranking model, Silhouette k-selection on XP biasing toward PPDB structure). These gaps mean the present synthesis cannot assert the magnitude, generality, or causal driver(s) of observed gains—only that the paper is promising but requires the specified additional quantitative and reproducibility evidence to resolve key uncertainties.

human_facing_meta_review.summary: The manuscript introduces SubstClus, a multi-view sense-clustering pipeline over PPDB that incorporates a Context Substitutability view (AddCos over sampled sentences), PPDB paraphrase scores, shared translations, and WordNet synset affinities via multi-view NMF. The authors evaluate inventories intrinsically with an extended B-Cubed F-score (β=0.5) against CoInCo lexsub annotations and extrinsically by using inventories to filter lexical substitution rankings (Syn.VSM, AddCos) under Unfiltered / Oracle / Best-Fit GAP settings. Results and qualitative examples indicate multi-view variants can produce useful, higher-coverage substitutable clusters and raise Oracle GAP substantially; realized Best-Fit gains are limited by WSD quality. Reviewers find the conceptual framing (making substitutability an explicit clustering view) and the extrinsic evaluation chain valuable, but they identify missing quantitative reporting, statistical testing, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, and reproducibility artifacts that limit assessment of effect sizes and robustness.
strengths: Clear task alignment: substitutability is operationalized formally via extended B-Cubed (β=0.5) and tied directly to lexical substitution evaluation.
Coherent multi-view design: combines context (AddCos), PPDB scores, translations, and WordNet affinity within a multi-view NMF framework to seek consensus clusters.
Practical extrinsic evaluation: inventories are applied as filters to real lexsub ranking models with Oracle and Best-Fit GAP measurements demonstrating downstream relevance.
Scalable engineering: uses PPDB2.0 and AGiga-trained embeddings and provides implementation-level detail (NMF objective, AddCos parameters) in appendices.
limitations: Missing per-inventory intrinsic substitutability numbers: the manuscript asserts SubstClus variants outperform baselines on B-Cubed but does not present an explicit numeric table of extended B-Cubed (β=0.5) values for each SubstClus variant and POS splits, preventing direct verification of C1.

No statistical tests or uncertainty estimates for GAP: reported Unfiltered/Oracle/Best-Fit GAP averages lack variance estimates, confidence intervals, or paired significance tests, so robustness and effect sizes of reported improvements are unclear.

Hyperparameter sensitivity unexamined: key operational choices (PPDB score cutoff = 2.3, XS sample size = 1000 sentences, λi = 0.01, k selection by Silhouette on XP) lack ablation/sensitivity analyses; results may depend on these heuristics (risk noted in A5/A6).

Inventory vs WSD confounding: Best-Fit GAP uses a simple WSD heuristic whose accuracy is not reported; Best-Fit results therefore conflate inventory quality with sense-disambiguation performance, obscuring how much benefit inventories alone provide.
open_questions: Please provide a table listing extended B-Cubed F-score (β=0.5) for every inventory evaluated (all SubstClus variants and baselines), with per-POS breakdowns and uncertainty estimates (e.g., bootstrap 95% CIs).
Can you report per-inventory coverage statistics analogous to Table 2 (|T|, average synonyms per target, average senses per target, average overlap with CoInCo) for all SubstClus variants?

Provide statistical testing for GAP: what are per-target GAP distributions and paired significance tests (e.g., paired bootstrap) comparing Unfiltered vs Best-Fit and vs Oracle for each inventory and ranking model?

What is the accuracy of the Best-Fit WSD heuristic (fraction of instances where it selects the oracle sense)? If feasible, can you report Best-Fit GAP when using a stronger WSD (supervised or contextual classifier) or a partial-oracle to disentangle inventory vs WSD effects?
consensus_snapshot: Reviewers agree the conceptual contribution—treating substitutability as an explicit context-derived clustering view and integrating it into multi-view NMF—is sensible and potentially useful for lexical substitution.
All reviewers find the extrinsic evaluation (inventories used to filter lexsub rankings, measuring Oracle and Best-Fit GAP) appropriate and valuable as a demonstration of practical utility.

There is broad consensus that the manuscript currently lacks several quantitative and reproducibility elements necessary to validate effect sizes and robustness (per-variant B-Cubed tables, coverage stats, statistical tests, hyperparameter sensitivity, WSD accuracy).
disagreement_snapshot: Degree of novelty: some reviewers emphasize the novelty of making substitutability a dedicated clustering view and view the contribution as an important reframing; others treat the work as an incremental engineering integration of existing components (multi-view NMF, AddCos, PPDB).

Confidence in empirical magnitude: reviewers differ on how convincing the presented GAP tables are without statistical tests—some regard reported Oracle gains as promising evidence, others judge the missing variance/statistics as a serious barrier to assessing magnitude and generality.
uncertainty_snapshot: Absence of numeric per-variant B-Cubed values prevents confirming intrinsic substitutability improvement claims and measuring effect sizes.
Without variance estimates or significance tests, it is uncertain which GAP improvements are robust across targets and which are sample- or target-specific.
Sensitivity of results to PPDB cutoff, AddCos sampling size, λi, and k-selection method is unknown; these hyperparameters may materially affect clustering and downstream performance.

The predictive relationship between substitutability (B-Cubed) and Oracle/Best-Fit GAP is asserted qualitatively but lacks quantified correlation coefficients and confidence intervals, leaving its strength unclear.

human_facing_meta_review.comments:
Summary: The manuscript describes SubstClus, a multi-view NMF pipeline that integrates a context-derived substitutability view (AddCos over sampled sentences) with PPDB paraphrase scores, shared translations, and WordNet affinities to produce substitutable paraphrase sense clusters from PPDB. Evaluation ties intrinsic substitutability (extended B-Cubed β=0.5) to extrinsic lexsub utility by filtering lexsub rankings (Syn.VSM, AddCos) and measuring GAP under Unfiltered / Oracle / Best-Fit conditions. Results and qualitative examples indicate promising Oracle gains and that multi-view variants can outperform automatic baselines.
Strengths: The work aligns the clustering goal explicitly with substitutability, uses a sensible multi-view design, and demonstrates downstream utility via lexsub filtering; engineering choices support scalability and appendices add implementation detail.
Limitations: (1) Missing per-variant numeric substitutability (extended B-Cubed) tables prevents direct verification of intrinsic claims; (2) GAP results lack variance estimates and statistical tests so robustness is unclear; (3) hyperparameter sensitivity (PPDB cutoff, XS sample size, λi, k-selection) is not studied and may materially affect outcomes; (4) Best-Fit conflates inventory quality with WSD heuristic performance—the heuristic’s accuracy is unreported. These limitations are concrete and tied to the manuscript’s reported experiments and claims.
Open Questions: (1) Please publish a full table of extended B-Cubed (β=0.5) per inventory (all SubstClus variants and baselines) with POS splits and CIs; (2) Provide coverage/overlap statistics per SubstClus variant analogous to Table 2; (3) Report per-target GAP distributions and paired statistical tests comparing Unfiltered vs Best-Fit and vs Oracle; (4) Quantify Best-Fit WSD accuracy and, if possible, report results when using a stronger WSD or a partial-oracle to separate inventory vs WSD effects.
Transparency: The manuscript documents many implementation details (NMF objective, AddCos details, PPDB cutoff rationale), which aids reproducibility. However, core artifacts and quantitative tables are missing: per-variant B-Cubed numbers, coverage tables, hyperparameter sweeps, WSD accuracy, and the actual SubstClus inventories and sampled sentences. Release of these artifacts and inclusion of requested analyses are necessary for verification.

confidence_interval.rationale: Moderate epistemic confidence that the multi-view substitutability framing and pipeline produce meaningful improvements under the described experimental setup (supported by Oracle GAP gains and coherent design). Confidence is reduced by missing quantitative per-variant intrinsic metrics, lack of statistical testing, untested hyperparameter sensitivity, and unreported WSD accuracy; these gaps materially affect claims about effect size, robustness, and generality. The interval reflects that while the approach is promising, the empirical strength and reproducibility require the concrete analyses and artifact release requested above.
